skill.name: personwise-security-awareness-training
skill.description: Creates grounded, interactive security awareness courses from supplied policies and training materials through the PersonWise service.
skill.summary: Turn security policies into an interactive digital-human awareness course with review checkpoints and controlled publication.
skill.author: personwiseai

security_audit.summary: Two static network findings are confirmed because the bootstrap installs opaque vendor executables that this audit cannot inspect. The remaining 140 static matches are false positives involving Markdown formatting, defensive installer operations, or signed descriptor data. Semantic review also found unvalidated service-supplied command execution and sensitive-document upload risks.

remediation.issue: Bootstrap scripts install executable binaries that are outside the audited skill source.
remediation.suggestion: Publish auditable source or reproducible builds, scan each binary, and verify an independent platform or minisign signature before installation.

remediation.issue: The workflow executes an update action returned by the remote service.
remediation.suggestion: Parse structured update fields into a fixed argv allowlist. Reject shell metacharacters, unexpected executables, origins, flags, and paths.

remediation.issue: Selected policy documents are uploaded to an external service.
remediation.suggestion: Display the destination and exact files before upload, require informed confirmation for sensitive materials, and document storage and retention controls.

semantic_findings.title: External Upload of Potentially Sensitive Policies

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source-add workflow and upload language directly confirm remote transmission; user selection limits scope but does not remove confidentiality risk.

high_findings.title: Unvalidated Service-Supplied Command Execution
high_findings.description: The skill tells the agent to run the exact update action returned by the PersonWise service after approval. Without an argv allowlist, a compromised response could supply an arbitrary shell command.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction to execute the returned action exactly is explicit, while no command grammar or metacharacter rejection is defined.

medium_findings.title: External Upload of Potentially Sensitive Policies
medium_findings.description: The workflow uploads every user-selected source document to PersonWise. Security policies and incident procedures can contain sensitive internal information, so this creates a material data-egress boundary.
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source-add workflow and upload language directly confirm remote transmission; user selection limits scope but does not remove confidentiality risk.

content.value_statement: Security policies are difficult to convert into clear employee training. This skill creates a grounded, interactive PersonWise course from supplied materials.
actual_capabilities: Builds a security awareness course from user-supplied policies, documents, text, and selected images.
Adapts course length to the live PersonWise account limit and the requested learner audience.
Creates private courses by default unless the user requests broader access.
Reviews outlines, scripts, source processing, images, and publication state at defined checkpoints.
Supports course creation, refinement, repair, publication, access changes, and status queries.
Returns run identifiers, source states, completion status, access mode, and the appropriate course URL.
limitations: Requires PersonWise CLI 1.1.6 or newer, browser OAuth, network access, and an eligible PersonWise account.
Uploads selected source materials to PersonWise for course processing.
Cannot guarantee security, certify employee competence, or replace technical security training.
Must remain grounded in supplied materials and cannot invent policies, statistics, incidents, or reporting procedures.

use_cases.title: Train New Employees
use_cases.description: Convert approved security policies into a concise private course covering recognition, response, and reporting.

use_cases.title: Refresh Department Guidance
use_cases.description: Create role-specific awareness training from current procedures for teams facing distinct security risks.

use_cases.title: Publish Compliance Support
use_cases.description: Prepare a reviewed awareness course for controlled internal sharing without claiming external certification.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Course
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a private security awareness course from [policy file] for [audience]. Focus on recognizing threats and using the documented reporting channel.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner course creation from one approved policy.

prompt_templates.title: Set Course Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [page count]-page security awareness course from [materials]. Cover [topics], use [language], and keep every factual claim grounded.
prompt_templates.scenario: Course creation with explicit length, topics, and language.

prompt_templates.title: Use Materials Only
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a materials-only course from [documents] for [audience]. Include recognition, response, reporting, and a short understanding check.
prompt_templates.scenario: Strictly grounded training from several internal documents.

prompt_templates.title: Review and Publish
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume course [project identifier], verify every source and checkpoint, correct unsupported content, then publish with [private or link] access.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced recovery, quality review, and controlled publication.

output_examples.input: Create a five-page private course from our phishing and incident-reporting policies.
output: Sources: phishing policy ready; incident-reporting policy ready.
Review: outline and script passed grounded-content checks.
Delivery: editor link returned after playability verification.

output_examples.input: Turn our remote-work security guide into awareness training for contractors.
output_examples.output: Created a contractor-focused course covering device care, suspicious messages, approved access, and the documented reporting path. The course remains private.

output_examples.input: Publish the reviewed course for anyone with the link and report its final status.
output_examples.output: The course completed successfully, link access is enabled, and the returned share link is ready for distribution.

best_practices: Provide current, approved policies and identify the intended learner audience.
Specify the desired access mode, page count, language, and required reporting channel.
Review sensitive documents before authorizing their upload to PersonWise.
anti_patterns: Do not request invented breach stories, threat statistics, policies, or reporting procedures.
Do not present course completion as security certification or proof of practical competence.
Do not upload unrelated files, secrets, credentials, or documents without clear authorization.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates an interactive digital-human course in PersonWise with slides, grounded voice questions, and optional understanding checks.

faq.question: What source materials can I provide?
faq.answer: You can provide approved policies, awareness documents, supplied text, and explicitly selected reference images.

faq.question: Does it upload my documents?
faq.answer: Yes. Selected source documents are uploaded to PersonWise for processing, so review confidentiality and authorization before use.

faq.question: Can it guarantee that employees are secure?
faq.answer: No. It supports awareness and reporting behavior but cannot eliminate risk, certify competence, or replace a security team.

faq.question: What access mode does it use?
faq.answer: New courses default to private access. Link access is used only when the user requests broader sharing.

faq.question: What account setup is required?
faq.answer: You need PersonWise CLI 1.1.6 or newer, browser OAuth, network access, and enough existing course credits.
